title: What If Mars Had Kept Its Magnetic Field?

scenes.text: What if Mars had kept its magnetic field? Today it loses air every single second.
The solar wind strips about 100 grams of gas from Mars every second, mostly carbon dioxide and oxygen.
Mars's global magnetic field shut down between 3.7 and 4.2 billion years ago. Then its air began to thin.
Today the atmosphere is just under one percent as thick as Earth's. Water can't stay liquid on the surface.
Back then the stripping ran 100 to 1,000 times faster, and solar storms boost it 10 to 20 times more.
A lasting shield might have kept thicker air and rivers. Earth still has one. Mars lost it, and the sky went with it.

description:
What if Mars had kept its magnetic field?
NASA's MAVEN shows the solar wind strips about 100 grams of gas from Mars each second, and the planet's field shut down more than 3.7 billion years ago.
